title_en: Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop v. Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, and Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd. — dispute over land debt-repayment contract (with third party Zhang Qixin)
ruling_gist_en: A pawnshop that holds a Financial Institution Legal Person License issued by the People's Bank of China, with its business scope including the provision of pledge loan services to non-state-owned small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals, is a legally established financial institution approved by the authorities. Where an actor obtains legal formalities for acquiring land and uses such land as collateral to borrow from the pawnshop, this does not violate the prohibitive provisions of relevant laws. Even if the land mortgage is not registered with the relevant authorities, this merely results in the mortgage having no legal effect against third parties, and does not affect the legal validity of the pawn agreement between the actor and the pawnshop.

full_text_en:
Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop v. Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, and the Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd., and Third Party Zhang Qixin — dispute over land debt repayment contract

[Ruling Summary]

A pawnshop that holds a financial institution legal person license issued by the People's Bank of China, with its business scope including handling pledge loan businesses for non-state-owned small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals, is a legally approved and established financial institution. Where an actor uses legally obtained land documentation as collateral to borrow from the pawnshop, it does not violate any prohibitive provisions of relevant laws. Even if the land mortgage has not been registered with the relevant authorities, it only fails to have legal effect against third parties, and does not affect the legality and validity of the pawn agreement between the actor and the pawnshop.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

No. 10 (2006) Min Er Ti Zi

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop (formerly Lufeng City Pawn Service Firm), domiciled at No. 68 Nanti Road, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Jinzhen, Manager.

Agent ad litem: Lin Youqi, Deputy Manager.

Agent ad litem: Gao Wei, Attorney at Beijing Rongbo Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Chen Weiping, male, 47 years old, Han ethnicity, former Chairman of the Board of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd., residing at No. 2, Pujiu Lane, opposite Youca Street, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Lu Dengpan, Attorney at Guangdong Zhengming Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hu Chunfa, Manager of Lufeng City Tongda Fine Chemical Plant.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 104 Nanti Road, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, Guangdong Province.

Responsible Person: Zhuang Xiaomin, Group Leader.

Agent ad litem: Lu Dengpan, Attorney at Guangdong Zhengming Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hu Chunfa, Manager of Lufeng City Tongda Fine Chemical Plant.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chen Shuming, male, 55 years old, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 45 Shibi Road, Youdong Street, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Cai Zhenguo, Attorney at Guangdong Shengfang Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Zhang Qixin, male, 69 years old, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 5, Pujiu Lane, opposite Youdong Street, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Cai Zhenguo, Attorney at Guangdong Shengfang Law Firm.

In the case of Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop (hereinafter referred to as the Pawnshop) versus Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, the Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Liquidation Group), and Third Party Zhang Qixin concerning a dispute over a land debt repayment contract, the Pawnshop, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Shen Jian Min Zai Zi No. 11 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court, filed an application for retrial with this Court. On May 10, 2006, this Court rendered the civil ruling (2005) Min Yi Jian Zi No. 10-1, deciding to grant a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on June 28, 2006, to try this case. The Pawnshop's agents ad litem Lin Youqi and Gao Wei, the joint agents ad litem of Chen Weiping and the Liquidation Group, Lu Dengpan and Hu Chunfa, and the joint agents ad litem of Chen Shuming and Zhang Qixin, Cai Zhenguo, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Facts Found by the Court

On March 24, 1995, Chen Weiping, then Chairman of the Board of Lufeng County Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangle Company), entered into a pawn agreement with the Pawnshop, borrowing RMB 500,000 from the Pawnshop, and providing as collateral the land use right located on the north side of Wangyang Guangsan Highway, Donghai Town, Lufeng City. The parties agreed that the pawn service fee and storage fee would be 1.2%, and the pawn interest and insurance premium would be calculated at a monthly rate of 1.5%, with a loan term of two months. After the agreement was signed, Kangle Company delivered to the Pawnshop as pledge the State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908, where the land user was Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transportation Company, the approval transfer document Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) No. 001 issued by the Lufeng County Land Bureau, and the land transfer fee invoice Lu Fa Pi NO. 0001288. The Pawnshop paid Chen Weiping a loan of RMB 500,000. The signing representative of the Pawnshop signed the agreement and affixed the Pawnshop's seal, Chen Weiping signed the agreement, and guarantor Zhang Qixin signed as guarantor, undertaking to repay the loan in full upon maturity. After the loan period expired, the borrower Chen Weiping and the guarantor Zhang Qixin failed to repay the principal and interest.

On May 31, June 11, and June 22, 1993, Chen Shuming entered into three pawn agreements with the Pawnshop, borrowing RMB 1,000,000, RMB 3,000,000, and RMB 1,000,000 respectively from the Pawnshop. The same year, the parties agreed that the pawn service fee and storage fee would be calculated at 1.2%, and the pawn interest and insurance premium at 1.5%. For each of the three loans, Chen Shuming executed loan IOUs and delivered them to the Pawnshop for safekeeping. After the loan periods expired, Chen Shuming repaid the Pawnshop loan principals of RMB 500,000 and RMB 220,000 on June 15 and August 16 of the same year respectively, totaling RMB 720,000. On January 18, 1996, Chen Shuming used the land recovery proceeds of Kangle Company to repay RMB 3,700,000. After deduction, the remaining principal of RMB 580,000 and interest were adjudicated in a separate case.

On January 11, 1996, Kangle Company, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming entered into a "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" with the Pawnshop. The deed stated: "The party executing this land transfer deed is Kangle Company, handled by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, who originally purchased a piece of land transferred from Lufeng City East Sea Town Urban Construction and Development Company, with the State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908 and a document Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) No. 001 issued by the Lufeng County Land Bureau, located at the former site of the County Loading and Transportation Station on the north side of Guangshan Highway, Lucheng, with a use right area of 3,196 square meters and a building area of 794 square meters. Now, because Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming of the former Kangle Company borrowed mortgage loans from the Pawnshop that have remained unpaid for a long time, it is agreed through discussion that the said land shall be transferred at the current market price with a total appraised value of RMB 5,200,000 to the Pawnshop as recovery to repay the debts. The transfer shall be handled by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming in person, and at the same time the boundaries of the said land shall be delineated, and together with the deed, documents, and receipt formalities, shall be delivered to the Pawnshop for custody, with the ownership becoming forever that of the buyer. The title to the land is clear, with no overlapping prior transactions. If there are any other claims or interference, the seller shall be solely responsible for handling and resolving them. This is a voluntary and fair transfer and recovery by both parties, with no repudiation whatsoever, and the transfer is final and irrevocable; henceforth, the transferor and its affiliates shall have no grounds for dispute or claims for additional payment or redemption. To avoid disputes based on oral statements, this deed is hereby executed as evidence." Kangle Company, as the transferor, affixed its seal on the deed; the Pawnshop, as the transferee, affixed its seal; and Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, and witness Zhang Qixin all signed the deed. After the "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" was signed, Chen Weiping still delivered the deed, the approval document Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) No. 001 issued by the Lufeng County Land Bureau, the State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908, and the land transfer fee invoice Lu Fa Pi NO. 0001288 to the Pawnshop for pledge. On January 18, 1996, pursuant to the "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed," Chen Yongfu, on behalf of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, wrote a "Receipt" stating: "Received from Lufeng Pawnshop the total sum of RMB 5,200,000 for the purchase of a piece of land originally purchased by Kangle Company from East Sea Town Urban Construction and Development Company, of which Chen Weiping is allocated RMB 1,500,000 and Chen Shuming is allocated RMB 3,700,000." Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, and witness Zhang Qixin all signed the "Receipt," and the "Receipt" was kept by the Pawnshop. On the same day, after settlement between Chen Weiping and the Pawnshop regarding the RMB 1,500,000 allocated to Chen Weiping, after deducting his loan principal of RMB 500,000 and interest of RMB 128,700, the loan repayment of RMB 180,000 made on behalf of Chen Runji and Chen Runqian, and the payment of RMB 100,000 made by the Pawnshop to Chen Weiping on that day, the Pawnshop still owed Chen Weiping RMB 591,300. The Pawnshop accordingly wrote an IOU and gave it to Chen Weiping. Thereafter, Chen Weiping, accompanied by Zhang Qixin, using the IOU, withdrew money on the following dates: January 19, 1996, RMB 200,000; January 25, RMB 200,000; January 30, RMB 40,000; February 8, RMB 40,000; February 12, RMB 40,000; February 14, RMB 41,300; and February 15, RMB 30,000. Total withdrawals amounted to RMB 591,300. After all the money was withdrawn, the Pawnshop retrieved the IOU. Thus, the Pawnshop settled the land recovery payments with Kangle Company, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming. The above facts are confirmed by: the receipt, testimony of Chen Shuming, witness Zhang Qixin, and drafter Chen Yongfu; testimony of the Pawnshop's cashier and staff; and the Pawnshop's account book records, which corroborate each other.

According to the approval document Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) No. 001 issued by the Land Bureau of Lufeng County, the land transferred from Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transportation Company to Lufeng City East Sea Town Urban Construction and Development Company (hereinafter referred to as East Sea Development Company) was only 2,500 square meters, not the 3,196 square meters recorded in the state-owned land use certificate of Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transportation Company. East Sea Development Company transferred the land of 2,500 square meters to Kangle Company, and Kangle Company paid the land transfer fee to East Sea Development Company based on 2,500 square meters, as evidenced by the land transfer fee invoice No. Lu Fa Pi NO. 0001288.

It was also found that: Kangle Company obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong (1997) Zi No. 0002556/15220100908 for the 2,500 square meters of land involved in this case on July 16, 1997, and on September 29, 1998, used this certificate to register a use right mortgage with the Lufeng City Land Bureau, obtaining the Land Use Right Mortgage Certificate Lu Fu Di Ya (98) Zi No. 0019, as collateral for a loan of RMB 1,950,000 borrowed by Lufeng City Tongda Fine Chemical Plant (of which Chen Weiping was the responsible person) from the Agricultural Bank of China Lufeng City Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ABC Lufeng Sub-branch). On December 19, 2002, the Lufeng City Land Bureau published a notice in the Shanwei Daily revoking the original State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908 of Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transportation Company. In April 2003, the Pawnshop, on the grounds that the Lufeng City Land Bureau, without recovering the original State-owned Land Use Certificate, had issued a new State-owned Land Use Certificate to Kangle Company and a Land Use Right Mortgage Certificate to ABC Lufeng Sub-branch, and that such administrative procedures were illegal, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Lufeng City People's Court, requesting revocation of the above certificates issued by the Lufeng City Land Bureau. On October 28, 2003, the Lufeng City People's Court rendered the administrative judgment (2003) Lu Xing Chu Zi No. 4, holding that Kangle Company obtained the land use right through adjustment and exchange pursuant to the document Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) No. 001 of the Lufeng County Land Bureau; when Kangle Company applied for registration of the change of land use right for the 2,500 square meters located on the north side of Guangshan Highway, Lucheng, Donghai Town, Lufeng City, although it provided an agreement and approval documents, it did not provide the original land certificate for the land; although the Lufeng City Land Bureau published a notice revoking the original State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908 of Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transportation Company on December 19, 2002, this act was carried out after the certificate was issued to Kangle Company; therefore, the certificate issuance violated legal provisions and statutory procedures, and should be revoked. The Land Use Right Mortgage Certificate (98) Zi No. 0019 obtained by ABC Lufeng Sub-branch was based on the State-owned Land Use Certificate Lu Fu Guo Yong (1997) Zi No. 0002556/15220100908 obtained by Kangle Company; since the issuance of that certificate was illegal, the Land Use Right Mortgage Certificate should also be revoked. The Lufeng City Land Bureau, the Liquidation Group, and ABC Lufeng Sub-branch, dissatisfied with this judgment, appealed to the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court. On January 17, 2004, the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court rendered the administrative judgment (2003) Shan Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 20, upholding the first instance judgment.

It was also found that: Kangle Company was a Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise established in 1991, with Chen Weiping serving as both Chairman of the Board and General Manager. Because it failed to undergo annual inspection for 1997, its business license was revoked by the Shanwei Administration for Industry and Commerce in 1998. On March 30, 2000, a Liquidation Group was established to liquidate Kangle Company's claims and debts during its operation. The Pawnshop was a collectively-owned enterprise legal person established in 1991, holding a financial institution legal person license issued by the People's Bank of China, with its enterprise legal person business license stating its business scope as: using its own funds to handle pledge loan businesses for non-state-owned small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals. Because it failed to undergo annual inspection from 2000 to 2002, its business license was revoked by the Lufeng Administration for Industry and Commerce on December 31, 2003.

Because the actual area of the land used for debt repayment differed from the area stated in the debt repayment agreement, the Pawnshop filed a lawsuit with the Lufeng City People's Court of Guangdong Province, requesting that Chen Weiping, Chen Shuming, and others return the transfer payment.

The Lufeng City People's Court of Guangdong Province held after trial that: The pawn agreement dated March 24, 1995 between the Pawnshop and Chen Weiping, and the pawn agreements dated May 31, June 11, and June 22, 1993 between the Pawnshop and Chen Shuming, as well as the loan IOUs, represented the true intentions of both parties; the contents of the agreements complied with the relevant provisions of Document No. (91) Yue Yin Guan Zi No. 186 of the Guangdong Branch of the People's Bank of China, and should be valid. After Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming respectively borrowed money from the Pawnshop, they failed to repay on time. Chen Weiping used the 3,196 square meters of land, which was the collateral for the loan, valued at RMB 5,200,000 for the transfer, to repay the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming. Because Kangle Company, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming failed to handle the recovery and transfer procedures for the 696 square meters of land as agreed in the deed, the transfer of the 3,196 square meters could not be registered. Therefore, the invalidity of the deed due to violation of relevant state laws and regulations was primarily the responsibility of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming. The Pawnshop also had fault for signing the deed and making full payment without obtaining the transfer procedures for the 696 square meters of land. Since the "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" is invalid, the RMB 5,200,000 obtained by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming should be returned by Chen Weiping to the Pawnshop in the amount of RMB 1,500,000 plus interest, and by Chen Shuming in the amount of RMB 3,700,000 plus interest, with interest calculated in accordance with the pawn agreement. Kangle Company provided the land to Chen Weiping as loan collateral, and later voluntarily allowed the land to be recovered by the Pawnshop to repay the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, and delivered the relevant documents, State-owned Land Use Certificate, agreement, and invoice to the Pawnshop for possession, thereby facilitating the formation of the pawn agreement and the "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed." Subsequently, it failed to handle the land transfer and registration procedures, causing the "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" to be invalid. Kangle Company should bear the fault liability for compensation for losses. The receipt stated that Chen Weiping received RMB 1,500,000 to repay loans, and this amount was settled, as evidenced by the receipt dated January 18, 1996, and witness Zhang Qixin. Chen Weiping's claim that the Pawnshop refused to pay the remaining RMB 591,300 should be dismissed for lack of evidence. The "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" signed by the four parties stated that the party executing the land transfer deed was Kangle Company, and that Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming originally purchased a piece of land of 3,196 square meters for use, and through discussion agreed to transfer the land at a value of RMB 5,200,000 to the Pawnshop as recovery to repay debts. The receipt stated that Chen Weiping received RMB 1,500,000 and Chen Shuming received RMB 3,700,000, which served as evidence. Kangle Company's claim that the land in the deed was 2,500 square meters with a price of RMB 5,200,000, and that the Pawnshop forcibly deducted RMB 3,700,000 for Chen Shuming, was not supported by sufficient evidence and should not be adopted. Although Third Party Zhang Qixin signed as a guarantor on the pawn agreement, the pawn agreement had been modified to a debt repayment with land, which had been performed, and the Pawnshop did not assert claims against Zhang Qixin; therefore, Zhang Qixin's guarantor liability should be discharged. The court then entered the following judgment: 1. The "Land Recovery and Transfer Deed" signed by the Pawnshop, Kangle Company, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming is void and not protected by law; 2. Chen Weiping shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay the land payment of RMB 1,500,000 received from the Pawnshop plus interest (calculated at a monthly rate of 2.7% from January 18, 1996 until the date of full repayment); 3. The guarantor liability of Third Party Zhang Qixin for Chen Weiping's loan of RMB 500,000 is discharged; 4. Chen Shuming shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay the land payment of RMB 3,700,000 received from the Pawnshop plus interest (calculated at a monthly rate of 2.7% from January 18, 1996 until the date of full repayment); 5. Kangle Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability within the scope of the land price provided as collateral for Chen Weiping's loan from the Pawnshop. Court acceptance fee of RMB 36,000 shall be borne by Chen Weiping in the amount of RMB 10,500, by Chen Shuming in the amount of RMB 25,500, and the preservation fee of RMB 26,000 shall be borne by the Pawnshop. Chen Weiping and Kangle Company, dissatisfied, appealed to the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province.

The Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province rendered a civil judgment (2000) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zhong Zi No. 7 on November 2, 2000, holding that: The "Land Repurchase and Transfer Deed" represented the true intention of all parties, its content did not violate legal provisions, and thus the debt-repayment relationship was established. However, the deed specified a land use right area of 3,196 square meters, whereas Kangnai Company had purchased only 2,500 square meters and had not obtained the land use right certificate. The land user indicated in the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" mentioned in the deed was the Lufeng County No. 1 Loading and Transport Company, and the relevant documents had been delivered to the pawnshop for custody upon signing. Subsequently, a dispute arose over who should handle the 696-square-meter shortfall, rendering the contract unenforceable as the transfer procedures were not completed, and therefore the contract was void. The pawnshop was required to return the land and related rights certificates to Kangnai Company, and Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming were required to return RMB 5,200,000 to the pawnshop. Chen Weiping claimed he had not received RMB 591,300 from the pawnshop, but the outstanding amount of RMB 591,300 had been collected by him in seven installments, as evidenced by the pawnshop's cashier's accounting vouchers and witness testimony. Therefore, Chen Weiping's appeal ground was unfounded and not upheld. Chen Weiping further argued that the interest of RMB 128,700 on the original loan of RMB 500,000 constituted usurious interest and double counting. According to Article 17 of Document No. (91) Yue Yin Guan Zi No. 186 of the Guangdong Branch of the People's Bank of China, the agreed monthly interest rate of 2.7% did not exceed the limit, and setting off the unpaid interest against the land debt was also not improper. Chen Weiping also argued that his undertaking to repay the debts of Chen Runji and Chen Runqian was based on the premise of the land debt-repayment, and since the debt-repayment was not established, he should not bear the repayment obligation. Since the debts of Chen Runji and Chen Runqian had been transferred to Chen Weiping at the time of signing the "Land Repurchase and Transfer Deed," the original creditor-debtor relationship between Chen Runji, Chen Runqian, and the pawnshop was extinguished; thus the first instance judgment correctly imposed liability on Chen Weiping. The loan relationship between Chen Weiping and the pawnshop was extinguished upon the establishment of the land debt-repayment relationship. Chen Weiping's claim to return the original loan of RMB 500,000 based on the loan relationship lacked legal basis and was not supported. Because the transfer was void, the first instance judgment's order for Chen Weiping to return the amount obtained under the contract while also calculating interest at the rate stipulated in the pawn agreement was improper; interest should instead be calculated by reference to the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China. Kangnai Company was also at fault regarding the contract's invalidity, and the first instance judgment's order for it to bear compensation liability was not improper. The first instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and partially erroneous results, which should be corrected. Accordingly, the judgment was: 1. Affirm items 1, 3, and 5 of the first instance judgment and the allocation of litigation costs; 2. Amend item 2 of the first instance judgment to: Chen Weiping shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return RMB 1,500,000 and interest to the pawnshop (interest calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment at the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China); 3. Amend item 4 of the first instance judgment to: Chen Shuming shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return RMB 3,700,000 and interest to the pawnshop (interest calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment at the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China); 4. The pawnshop shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return to Kangnai Company the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" [Certificate No. Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908], Document No. Guo Fu Tu Han (1995) 001 from the Lufeng County Land Bureau, Invoice No. Lu Fa Pi NO.0001288, and one copy of the agreement signed between Kangnai Company and Donghai Development Company on January 1, 1996. Appeal costs of RMB 36,000 were to be borne by Chen Weiping and Kangnai Company each in the amount of RMB 9,000, and by the pawnshop in the amount of RMB 18,000. After the judgment, the Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate filed a protest with the Guangdong High People's Court on the grounds that the second instance judgment's findings of fact were based on insufficient key evidence. The Guangdong High People's Court, by letter (2002) Yue Gao Fa Li Shen Shen Zi No. 12, referred the case to the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province for retrial.

The Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province rendered a civil judgment (2002) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zai Zhong Zi No. 3 on June 7, 2002, holding that: The focus of this case was whether, after the parties signed the land repurchase and transfer deed, the pawnshop had paid Chen Weiping the land transfer price of RMB 591,300. According to the principle that he who asserts must prove, the pawnshop claimed that the outstanding amount was collected by Chen Weiping and Zhang Qixin in seven installments against an IOU. The evidence provided included a receipt for RMB 5,200,000 received by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, the pawnshop's internal cashier's ledger, and testimonies from the pawnshop's cashier and the intermediary witness, Zhang Qixin. Although the internal ledger violated the "Work Rules for Accounting Personnel" and "Basic Standards for Accounting Work," and lacked original documentation for Chen Weiping's seven withdrawals, the evidentiary value of other evidence—including the testimony of Zhang Qixin, who had no conflicting interest with either party, the receipt for RMB 5,200,000 signed by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, and the pawnshop's ledger—should be confirmed. This evidence was sufficient to prove that the pawnshop had fully paid Chen Weiping the RMB 591,300; therefore, the pawnshop's claim that the outstanding amount was repaid in seven installments should be upheld. Chen Weiping claimed he had not received the outstanding amount, but failed to produce valid evidence such as a balance IOU from the pawnshop, and had never demanded payment from the pawnshop before the pawnshop filed the lawsuit. Therefore, his claim was not upheld. Upon deliberation by the adjudication committee, the judgment was as follows: Dismiss the protest and affirm the second instance judgment. Chen Weiping and the liquidation team, dissatisfied, applied to the Guangdong High People's Court for retrial. The Guangdong High People's Court, by civil ruling (2004) Yue Gao Fa Shen Jian Min Zai Zi No. 11 on February 4, 2004, decided to bring the case up for trial.

The Guangdong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2004) Yue Gao Fa Shen Jian Min Zai Zi No. 11 on July 6, 2004, holding that: Kangnai Company used land use rights it had not yet acquired to repay the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming to the pawnshop, and the area did not match, nor were the relevant procedures lawfully completed or approved by the relevant authorities; therefore, the agreement should be confirmed as void. The parties were required to return the property and related rights certificates obtained, and the creditor-debtor relationship established under the original pawn agreement was thereby restored. The pawn objects under the four pawn agreements signed between the pawnshop and Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming were all IOUs or related rights certificates, which did not possess the general legal characteristics of pawn; therefore, the said agreements were contracts in the name of pawn but were in fact loans. The pawnshop, lacking qualification to engage in financial business, lent money to Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming, violating relevant financial laws and regulations, and should be confirmed as void. Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming should return the principal loan amounts of RMB 500,000 and RMB 3,500,000 respectively to the pawnshop, and pay interest calculated at the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China. Kangnai Company delivered relevant rights documents to the pawnshop as security for Chen Weiping's loan from the pawnshop, which should be deemed as establishing a mortgage relationship between Kangnai Company and the pawnshop. Because the pawn agreement was void, and Kangnai Company had not yet acquired the rights under the relevant documents at the time, the mortgage relationship should be confirmed as void, and Kangnai Company should bear liability for its fault. To the extent that Chen Weiping was unable to repay the RMB 500,000 and interest to the pawnshop, Kangnai Company should bear compensation liability within the value of the land use rights. Although the pawnshop did not explicitly request in its statement of claim that Kangnai Company be held liable, the pawnshop had named Kangnai Company as a defendant and requested the court to take preservation measures against its property; in subsequent proceedings, the pawnshop did actually request Kangnai Company to bear liability. Therefore, it could not be concluded that the original judgment exceeded the pawnshop's claims. However, the original judgment's division of the scope of Kangnai Company's liability was inappropriate and should be corrected. Regarding the scope of property to be returned by Chen Weiping, on January 18, 1996, Chen Weiping issued a receipt for the RMB 1,500,000 he had received, and both parties acknowledged that this receipt included the RMB 500,000 loan principal and its interest of RMB 128,700, RMB 100,000 paid after the agreement, and RMB 180,000 paid on behalf of Chen Runji and others. Chen Weiping did not receive the outstanding balance of RMB 591,300 on that day. Regarding this RMB 591,300, the original judgment found that the pawnshop had fully paid Chen Weiping, with the main evidence being the pawnshop's internal cash flow ledger, the cashier's testimony, and Zhang Qixin's testimony. However, the cash flow ledger was an internal record of the pawnshop, the cashier was also an employee of the pawnshop, and Zhang Qixin, who was both a guarantor under the original pawn agreement and an intermediary witness in the debt-repayment, had an interest in this case. Chen Weiping also denied receipt. Therefore, the basis for the original judgment's finding that Chen Weiping had received the RMB 591,300 was insufficient, and this court corrects it. However, Chen Weiping should return the RMB 100,000 delivered on January 18, 1996, and interest (calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment at the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China). During the performance of the debt-repayment agreement with the pawnshop, Chen Weiping voluntarily undertook to repay RMB 180,000 on behalf of Chen Runji and Chen Runqian to the pawnshop. This expression of intent was genuine and constituted a debt transfer contract formed between Chen Weiping and the pawnshop during the debt-repayment process. Because the debt-repayment agreement between Chen Weiping and the pawnshop was confirmed as void, Chen Weiping had not actually repaid the RMB 180,000 debt to the pawnshop. Therefore, Chen Weiping should return the RMB 180,000 and interest (calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment at the同期 loan interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China) to the pawnshop. The pawnshop did not sue Zhang Qixin, and the original court's judgment to release him from his guarantee liability exceeded the scope of the pawnshop's claims; this court corrects this. In summary, Chen Weiping and Kangnai Company's application for retrial was partially well-founded and supported. The original judgment was partially erroneous in fact-finding and improperly applied the law, which should be corrected. Accordingly, the judgment was: 1. Set aside the civil judgment (2002) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zai Zhong Zi No. 3 of the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court and the civil judgment (2000) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zhong Zi No. 7; 2. Set aside items 2, 3, 4, and 5 of the judgment (1998) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 205 of the Lufeng City People's Court; 3. Affirm item 1 of the judgment (1998) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 205 of the Lufeng City People's Court and the allocation of first instance litigation costs; 4. Chen Weiping shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return RMB 780,000 and interest to the pawnshop (for RMB 500,000, interest calculated from March 24, 1995, until the date of full repayment; for RMB 280,000, interest calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment; both at the同期 loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China); 5. Chen Shuming shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return RMB 3,700,000 and interest to the pawnshop (interest calculated from January 18, 1996, until the date of full repayment at the同期 loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China); 6. Kangnai Company shall, within the value of the land use rights in this case, bear compensation liability for the principal and interest of the RMB 500,000 loan from the pawnshop to Chen Weiping; 7. The pawnshop shall, within 10 days of this judgment taking effect, return to Kangnai Company the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" [Certificate No. Lu Fu Guo Yong Zong Zi No. 0002556 (1992) No. 15220100908], Document No. Guo Fu Tu Han (1995) 001 from the Lufeng County Land Bureau, Invoice No. Lu Fa Pi NO.0001288, and one copy of the agreement signed between Kangnai Company and Donghai Development Company on January 1, 1996. Second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 36,000 was to be borne by Chen Weiping in the amount of RMB 5,000, Kangnai Company in the amount of RMB 9,000, and the pawnshop in the amount of RMB 22,000.

The pawnshop applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: 1. The Guangdong High People's Court retrial judgment's finding that the pawn agreements between the pawnshop and Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming were void lacked legal basis. The pawnshop was a lawfully established financial institution, and the loan conduct was the true intention of both parties, not violating laws or regulations; therefore, the contracts should be valid. The retrial judgment's finding that the agreements were in the name of pawn but were in fact loans was inconsistent with the facts. Kangnai Company's use of the land it purchased to repay the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming and the delivery of valid certificates to the pawnshop for custody was its true intention, did not violate the law, and should be deemed valid. As for the discrepancy between the area stated in the debt-repayment agreement and the actual area, the part corresponding to the actual area should be deemed valid, and the inaccuracy as to the area did not affect the validity of the actual area. When Kangnai Company used the land to repay the debt, although registration procedures had not been completed, the title holder and relevant competent authorities raised no objection. In fact, Kangnai Company had registered the land in its own name on July 16, 1997, according to the actual area of 2,500 square meters. The failure to register the remaining 696 square meters was not a problem with the debt-repayment agreement itself, but was due to intentional breach of contract by Chen Weiping and the Kangnai Company under his control. 2. The Guangdong High People's Court retrial judgment's finding that Chen Weiping had not received the RMB 591,300 paid by the pawnshop lacked factual basis. Multiple witness testimonies and original accounting records provided by the pawnshop proved that Chen Weiping had withdrawn the RMB 591,300 in seven installments, and the original IOU was torn up in the presence of both parties. Given that Chen Weiping could not produce the original IOU, the finding that he had not received this amount lacked basis. 3. The Guangdong High People's Court retrial judgment's failure to find that Kangnai Company should bear compensation liability for fault in contracting violated the rules.

Chen Weiping and the liquidation team defended, arguing: 1. The pawnshop did not pay Chen Weiping the RMB 591,300. If it claimed to have performed the payment obligation, it bore the burden of proof and should produce a receipt from Chen Weiping; otherwise, it should bear the consequences of failure of proof. The pawnshop, without a receipt to support its claim, submitted evidence such as internal cash flow ledgers, cashier testimony, Zhang Qixin's testimony, and other testimonies, which were clearly insufficient as proof. Even if it were accepted that the pawnshop had paid the above amount in seven installments, the payment was not made to Chen Weiping but to Zhang Qixin. 2. The "Land Repurchase and Transfer Deed" should be deemed void, and Kangnai Company should not bear liability for fault. At the time Kangnai Company valued its land use rights and transferred them to the pawnshop to offset the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming to the pawnshop, it did not possess the land use rights. Although it obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for the land on July 16, 1997, this certificate's acquisition had been revoked by the effective administrative judgment (2003) Shan Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 20 of the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court because it was obtained illegally. Even if Kangnai Company had rights to the land, the transfer of rights would require approval from the superior competent authorities and the state-owned assets department to be valid; the debt-repayment area was short by 696 square meters, for which Kangnai Company had no documentation. The primary fault for the contract's invalidity lay with the pawnshop. After the deed was signed, the pawnshop failed to perform its payment obligation as agreed; before signing the deed, the pawnshop knew of the 696-square-meter discrepancy and knew who was to handle the procedures for that area, and after signing, it lent Chen Shuming RMB 250,000 to handle the relevant procedures. Since the procedures were never completed, and the land price significantly dropped in the meantime, the pawnshop reneged and was unwilling to continue performing the deed. Even if the fault for the deed's invalidity lay with Kangnai Company and it should bear compensation liability for fault in contracting, the pawnshop must have suffered actual loss. However, after the deed was voided, the pawnshop could still exercise its creditor's rights against Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming. The pawnshop had no reason to make Kangnai Company bear joint liability for Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming's debts. At the time of filing the lawsuit, the pawnshop did not request Kangnai Company to bear joint liability for Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming's debts; the retrial's change to the original claim was procedurally improper. 3. The pawn agreements signed between the pawnshop and Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming should also be deemed void. According to relevant pawn industry regulations, the pawn object must be movable property or tangible items, not including negotiable instruments or rights certificates. In this case, the pawn objects under the pawn agreements were all IOUs and related certificates, which did not possess the general legal characteristics of pawn. They were in the name of pawn but were in fact credit loans. Since pawnshops are not permitted to engage in credit loan business, the pawn agreements signed with Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming should all be deemed void. In conclusion, the original judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law and should be affirmed.

Chen Shuming defended, arguing: The 2,500-square-meter land was actually purchased with funds provided by himself and with Chen Weiping handling the procedures; therefore, the actual owners of the land were Chen Shuming and Chen Weiping jointly, not Kangnai Company. Kangnai Company was merely the nominal owner. The land debt-repayment conduct in this case was lawful and valid, the 2,500-square-meter land had already become the property of the pawnshop, and Chen Shuming had already fully offset the RMB 3,700,000 debt to the pawnshop. He requested a judgment confirming the validity of the land debt-repayment conduct and ordering that the land be used to repay the pawnshop.

Zhang Qixin defended, arguing: The "Land Repurchase and Transfer Deed" was the true intention of all parties, did not violate laws or regulations, and should be valid. The RMB 591,300 that the pawnshop owed Chen Weiping was withdrawn by Chen Weiping from the pawnshop in seven installments in the presence of the defender. The pawnshop recorded the repayment amount on the IOU after each payment, and after the final withdrawal, Chen Weiping returned the IOU to the pawnshop. He requested the setting aside of the original judgment and that the 2,500-square-meter land in this case be used to repay the pawnshop.

This Court holds that the pawnshop held a Financial Institution Legal Person Permit issued by the People's Bank of China, and its business scope included handling pledge loans for non-state-owned small and medium-sized enterprises and individuals; it was a lawfully established financial institution. Although Chen Weiping's loan from the pawnshop was secured by the lawful procedures for Kangnai Company's acquisition of the land, this did not violate any prohibitive provisions of law. Although the land mortgage was not registered with the relevant authorities, this only meant it was not effective against third parties and did not affect the validity of the pawn agreements signed between the pawnshop and Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming.

Although Kangnai Company, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming agreed with the Pawnshop in the Land Recovery and Transfer Deed that Kangnai Company would use its 3,196 square meters of land valued at RMB 5.2 million to offset the debts owed by Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming to the Pawnshop, according to the approval document No. Lu Guo Tu Han (1995) 001 from the Lufeng County Land Bureau and the invoice for the land transfer payment, the actual area of land that Kangnai Company acquired by transfer was only 2,500 square meters, of which the Pawnshop should have been aware. The procedures for Kangnai Company's acquisition of the 2,500 square meters of land from Donghai Development Company were lawful. Its use of this 2,500 square meters of land to offset the debts of Chen Weiping and Chen Shuming to the Pawnshop represents the true intention of all parties and does not violate legal provisions; therefore, it should be deemed valid and should continue to be performed. The transfer of the land area exceeding 2,500 square meters in the Land Recovery and Transfer Deed, i.e., 696 square meters, lacks a lawful basis and should be deemed invalid.

Since Chen Weiping, when he issued the Receipt to confirm receipt of his allocated RMB 1.5 million, had not yet collected the remaining balance of RMB 591,300 after deductions, it is reasonable that the Pawnshop issued an IOU to Chen Weiping on the same day for him to keep. The Pawnshop's claim that it paid the remaining RMB 591,300 to Chen Weiping in seven installments, and that after the final payment, the IOU was retrieved from Chen Weiping and canceled, is supported by the Pawnshop's evidence: Chen Weiping's payment receipts, testimony of Chen Shuming, testimony of witness Zhang Qixin, testimony of the scrivener Chen Yongfu, and is sufficient to corroborate the testimony of the Pawnshop's cashier and staff, as well as the Pawnshop's ledger records. The above evidence corroborates each other and has sufficient probative value; this Court admits it. Since Chen Weiping admitted that the RMB 1.5 million in the payment receipt already included the RMB 591,300 that he had not yet collected, then when Chen Weiping later collects that amount, he does not need to issue another payment receipt. Chen Weiping argued in his defense that he did not receive the RMB 591,300 from the Pawnshop, but failed to provide corresponding evidence; therefore, this Court does not sustain his argument.

Given that the land use certificate for the 2,500 square meters of land has not yet been transferred to the name of the Pawnshop, the Liquidation Group, Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming shall continue to perform the obligations stipulated in the Land Recovery and Transfer Deed and assist the Pawnshop in handling the land use right formalities for the 2,500 square meters of land. In summary, the judgment of the original trial erred in fact-finding and improperly applied the law, and should be reversed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Reverse the civil judgment No. (2004) Yue Gao Fa Shen Jian Min Zai Zi No. 11 of the Guangdong High People's Court, the civil judgment No. (2002) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zai Zhong Zi No. 3 of the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, the civil judgment No. (2000) Shan Zhong Fa Jing Zhong Zi No. 7 of the Shanwei Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, and the civil judgment No. (1998) Lu Jing Chu Zi No. 205 of the Lufeng People's Court of Guangdong Province.

2. The Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd., Chen Weiping, and Chen Shuming shall continue to perform the obligation of using the 2,500 square meters of land to repay the debt as stipulated in the Land Recovery and Transfer Deed.

3. Dismiss the other claims of Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop.

The total case acceptance fees for the first and second instances amount to RMB 72,000, to be borne by the Liquidation Group of Lufeng City Kangle Dairy Products Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 24,000, by Chen Weiping in the amount of RMB 24,000, by Chen Shuming in the amount of RMB 12,000, and by Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop in the amount of RMB 12,000; the preservation fee for the first instance of RMB 26,000 is to be borne by Lufeng City Lufeng Pawnshop.

This judgment is final.
